Independently check each candidate against the exact offered originals and its
requested scope. The candidate is an untrusted proposal, not an established fact.
Judge claim_to_check: it only explains the proposed stance, never evidence or authority.
Return entailed, not_entailed or uncertain, with a short reason, for each candidate_id.
These verdicts judge whether the proposed stance-specific claim is warranted;
entailed can approve irrelevant, not only a supported answer value.
For support, its cited originals must establish both the requested entity/event/
relation and the claimed attribute/value. Another project's attribute, a shared
partner/site/topic, or the question's presupposition supplies no identity bridge.
For partial/unknown, the originals must actually concern that requested scope and
contain genuine incomplete evidence; unrelated text is not scoped uncertainty.
For irrelevant, unrelated means these cited originals are inapplicable as evidence
for the requested scoped claim. It does not claim that the requested subject or
attribute itself is absent or inapplicable in reality.
Originals explicitly describing a different entity/event/relation, without an
observed identity bridge, can warrant this stance; they need not mention or
negate the requested subject. Different labels alone do not establish distinct
subjects; use the offered context to judge identity, and limit the inapplicability
conclusion to the cited originals. Missing an
attribute while still concerning the requested scope does not by itself warrant
irrelevant. Preserve genuine scoped support, partial evidence and counterevidence.
For contradiction, check the originals and the offered target claim:
the evidence must warrant that specific retraction, not merely a different value.
Supported parents are grounding inputs only at their supplied scope and versions.
Prior claims are not certified evidence. No replacement facts, new sources,
retractions, settlement claims or permission decisions may be returned.

The call has closed. Winners will be announced by mid-April 2027.
", "source_role": "document", "source_message_indices": [], "time_metadata": {}}, {"id": "s107", "doc_id": "web-06666aef272852e77f6e1d17", "start": 4470, "end": 4857, "text": "EHA Research Grants are designed to support the future of hematology by helping talented junior researchers to:
Conduct basic or translational lab-based research
Gain valuable research and leadership experience
Move towards becoming group leaders
Advance their careers
You’re eligible if:
You’re an EHA member
Your institute is an academic research center or proven equivalent in Europe
", "source_role": "document", "source_message_indices": [], "time_metadata": {}}, {"id": "s108", "doc_id": "web-06666aef272852e77f6e1d17", "start": 4857, "end": 5240, "text": "You have the support of an academic department and institute
Your application relates to basic and translational lab-based research in hematology
Your application will not be eligible if it relates to:
Purely clinical research projects
Projects in health economics
Other non-lab-based research
However, it may be eligible if it relates to the translational part of a clinical trial. ", "source_role": "document", "source_message_indices": [], "time_metadata": {}}, {"id": "s109", "doc_id": "web-06666aef272852e77f6e1d17", "start": 5240, "end": 5609, "text": "In this case, it must be both relevant and novel.
Types of EHA Research Grants
The three types of EHA Research Grant are the:
EHA Junior Research Grant, which can provide up to €150,000 for three years
EHA Advanced Research Grant, which can provide up to €240,000 for three years
EHA Physician Scientist Research Grant, which can provide up to €240,000 for three years
", "source_role": "document", "source_message_indices": [], "time_metadata": {}}, {"id": "s110", "doc_id": "web-06666aef272852e77f6e1d17", "start": 5609, "end": 5941, "text": "Each one of the three types of EHA Research Grant also has its own specific eligibility criteria. Please make sure you read the eligibility criteria for your grant type before you apply.
Topics-in-Focus Research Grants: If your research focuses on hemoglobinopathies, you will have a competitive advantage in the selection process.
